reviews.reason: The broad-capability REST chain is real, and the Phase 3a line mismatch is a sink-location issue rather than a hallucinated code path because `cloud_save_and_test()` exists at `src/StorageProviders/API/Rest.php:262` and `job_run_archive()` starts at `inc/class-destination-s3.php:447`. I recommend keeping the finding `UNCERTAIN` because the end-to-end disclosure claim still needs runtime proof that a `backwpup_check` user can complete the multi-request flow and that the resulting archive actually lands in attacker-controlled S3, not just that bounded S3 fields were written into `backwpup_jobs`.

counter_evidence.detail: The legacy S3 AJAX editor is not open to the read-only role: `edit_ajax()` aborts unless the caller has `backwpup_jobs_edit` and a valid `backwpup_ajax_nonce`.

The backup start path only proceeds when at least one configured destination passes `can_run()`, so the REST capability mismatch alone does not prove that arbitrary S3 values immediately produce a successful upload.

For S3, `can_run()` only returns true when stored credentials include both `s3accesskey` and `s3secretkey`; the code review therefore shows state change, but not verified bucket ownership or successful object creation.

missing_evidence: Need a captured low-privilege run showing that the same `backwpup_check` session can call `/wp-json/backwpup/v1/cloudsaveandtest`, `/wp-json/backwpup/v1/updatejob`, and `/wp-json/backwpup/v1/startbackup` with a valid `X-WP-Nonce` and an existing file-producing job ID.

Need end-to-end proof that the chosen job actually produces a backup file and that `BackWPup_Destination_S3::job_run_archive()` uploads that archive into the attacker-controlled bucket, rather than only storing credentials in `backwpup_jobs`.

Need request-shape confirmation that the exploit uses form-encoded parameters, because `BackWPup_Destination_S3::edit_form_post_save()` consumes `$_POST` at `inc/class-destination-s3.php:163-243` instead of reading the `WP_REST_Request` object directly.
dynamic_test_plan: Step 1: Create at least one existing BackWPup job that produces a file archive, create a tester-controlled S3 bucket, and assign a second user the shipped `backwpup_check` role.

Step 2: Log in as the `backwpup_check` user, open a BackWPup admin page, capture `backwpupApi.nonce`, and obtain a real job ID from the job-card markup exposed under the broad `backwpup` permission, for example the `data-job-id` attributes rendered in `components/job-item.php:86-92` and `components/job-item.php:150-154`.

Step 3: Send a form-encoded `POST /wp-json/backwpup/v1/cloudsaveandtest` with header `X-WP-Nonce: <nonce>` and body fields such as `cloud_name=s3`, `job_id=<jobid>`, `s3accesskey=<attacker key>`, `s3secretkey=<attacker secret>`, `s3bucket=<attacker bucket>`, `s3region=<region>`, and `s3dir=loot/`; then verify in the database or UI that the target job's S3 settings inside site option `backwpup_jobs` changed.

Step 4: Send a form-encoded `POST /wp-json/backwpup/v1/updatejob` with `job_id=<jobid>` and `storage_destinations[]` containing the existing destinations plus `S3`, then send `POST /wp-json/backwpup/v1/startbackup` with the same `job_id` and the captured `X-WP-Nonce`.

Step 5: Verify measurable impact by confirming a new archive appears in the attacker bucket and, if needed, by checking the BackWPup log for the `Backup transferred to ...` message emitted from `inc/class-destination-s3.php:679-685`.

reviews.reason: The REST bulk-delete route and local-folder delete sink are both real, and the Phase 3a mismatch is again a sink-location correction because `process_bulk_actions()` starts at `src/Backups/API/Rest.php:360` while `BackWPup_Destination_Folder::file_delete()` starts at `inc/class-destination-folder.php:62`. I recommend keeping the finding `UNCERTAIN` because the ordinary backups UI does withhold a ready-made delete payload from users lacking `backwpup_backups_delete`, but the same low-privileged user still appears able to derive the needed `job_id`, destination, and filename from backups-list HTML returned under the broader `backwpup` permission.

counter_evidence.detail: The new backups UI does not directly hand `backwpup_check` a delete URL: `dataset-delete` is only populated when the current user already has `backwpup_backups_delete`.

The checkbox payload comes from `json_encode( $backup['dataset-delete'] ?? null )`, so a stock bulk-delete click from a non-deleter should submit `null` and then fail the REST handler's `data-url` requirement instead of deleting immediately.

The reviewed sink is constrained to the configured backup directory and a basename-resolved real path before `wp_delete_file()` runs, so this path is backup-archive deletion rather than arbitrary file deletion.

missing_evidence: Need a captured `backwpup_check` response from `POST /wp-json/backwpup/v1/backups` proving that the running product really returns enough DOM metadata to reconstruct `jobdest-top` and the target filename when `dataset-delete` is omitted.

Need an end-to-end request/response pair showing that the stock UI bulk-delete attempt fails for `backwpup_check`, while a manually crafted `process_bulk_actions` request with a synthetic `data-url` succeeds.

Need a runtime check confirming the deleted archive actually disappears from the target storage and backup list, because the static review only proves the handler reaches `file_delete()` when given a valid query string.
dynamic_test_plan: Step 1: Create at least one local `FOLDER` backup archive, activate the plugin, and assign a second user the shipped `backwpup_check` role.

Step 2: Log in as that user, capture `backwpupApi.nonce`, and send `POST /wp-json/backwpup/v1/backups` with `page=1&length=10`; inspect the returned HTML for the always-generated download dataset that includes `data-jobid`, `data-destination`, and `data-file` via `inc/Utils/BackWPupHelpers.php:163-172`.
Step 3: Try the normal bulk-delete UI once and confirm the request fails or returns per-item errors, because `dataset-delete` is omitted for roles without `backwpup_backups_delete`.

Step 4: Manually send `POST /wp-json/backwpup/v1/process_bulk_actions` with header `X-WP-Nonce: <nonce>` and a form body like `action=delete&backups[0][dataset][data-url]=/wp-admin/admin.php?page=backwpupbackups&action=delete&jobdest-top=<jobid>_<DEST>&backupfiles[]=<filename>`; note that the REST handler only parses the query string at `src/Backups/API/Rest.php:401-410` and does not verify the legacy `_wpnonce` parameter from that URL.
Step 5: Verify impact by confirming the selected archive disappears from the backups list and from the configured backup directory on disk.
